human_actions_pending.action: Choose the fix path at 06-13 Task 1 (checkpoint:decision, gate=blocking)
human_actions_pending.context: Three options against 06-12's profile: reduce-request-cost (reversible), reduce-threads (costly), add-workers (ONE-WAY). add-workers is one-way because _db_lock is a module-global threading.Lock (dashboard/app.py:127), so a second gunicorn worker is a second interpreter with a second independent lock against one SQLite file - granting unserialized cross-process write access while T-06-24's diff-based closure evidence still passes. PROH-OPS-04-05 names this.

context_notes: Wave 1 was 06-11 and 06-12 in parallel isolated worktrees - the first genuinely disjoint pair in this phase (zero files_modified intersection). Base SHA for both worktrees is f672832. 06-11 reported 15-16 full-suite failures under concurrent load, all in test_advanced_ui.py / test_history_investigation_ui.py / test_ui_states.py, all passing in isolation - attributed to Playwright/Chromium contention from the sibling agent. That attribution is plausible but UNVERIFIED on a quiet tree; the 837/561 floor is an acceptance criterion, so re-run it before trusting the number. The one plan constraint most likely to be lost during 06-13's implementation is its unconditional row-bound clause: /api/services must stay bounded in rows read per request on whatever path it uses, because the existing test_the_bulk_read_is_bounded guards the repository layer and would stay green while the route lost its cap.
